title: An Empirical Analysis of Parameter-Efficient Methods for Debiasing Pre-Trained Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical bias by evaluating a model's preference for a stereotypical sentence over a less-stereotypical one in a given pair of sentences related to religious contexts.
findings: Parameter-efficient debiasing methods (prefix tuning, prompt tuning, adapter tuning) combined with Counterfactual Data Augmentation (CDA) are less effective at mitigating religious and racial bias compared to gender bias. Post-hoc debiasing methods like SelfDebias showed superior performance in reducing religious bias. This reduced effectiveness is potentially due to the bias attribute word lists for religion being shorter and containing more noisy or ambiguous terms compared to the lists for gender, which undermines the quality of the augmented training data.
